summary: Kernel optimization is essential for efficient large language model (LLM) training and inference on Ascend NPUs. Existing Ascend kernel benchmarks primarily focus on kernel generation, with less emphasis on the ability of agents to optimize existing implementations under input configurations drawn from real workloads.
takeaways: Existing Ascend kernel benchmarks primarily focus on kernel generation, with less emphasis on the ability of agents to optimize existing implementations under input configurations drawn from real workloads.
In terms of usability, two evaluation modes are supported in AscendGYM: model evaluation and model-harness evaluation.
The kernel optimization capabilities of both trained models and custom agents are allowed to be measured.
